name: Multiple Pterygium Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Multiple Pterygium Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of multiple webbing (pterygia) across major joints
Characteristic facial features including ptosis, micrognathia, and cleft palate
Respiratory difficulties due to thoracic cage abnormalities
Identification of pathogenic mutations in CHRNG or related genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple pterygia, congenital joint contractures, and characteristic facial dysmorphism
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

searchTerms: multiple skin webs over major joints
webbing of skin across elbows and knees
excess skin folds on large joints
joint contractures present at birth
multiple stiff joints from birth
arthrogryposis with limited joint movement

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic facial dysmorphism including ptosis and micrognathia
searchTerms: facial features with drooping eyelids and small jaw
distinctive face shape including ptosis and micrognathia
characteristic facial appearance with eyelid droop

common.symptomName: Thoracic cage deformities leading to restrictive lung disease
searchTerms: chest bone deformities causing breathing difficulty
abnormal rib cage restricting lung expansion
thoracic cage shape causing lung problems
undescended testicles
testes not in scrotum
hidden testicles at birth

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory infections secondary to restrictive lung disease
searchTerms: lung infections due to restricted breathing
frequent respiratory infections from lung problems
breathing-related infections caused by chest deformities
trouble feeding as baby
difficulty sucking or swallowing
infant feeding problems
late crawling or walking
delayed movement skills
slow motor development

laboratory: Genetic testing identifying mutations in CHRNG, CHRNA1, or related genes
imaging: X-rays showing joint contractures and pterygia
Chest X-ray demonstrating thoracic cage deformities
genetic: Autosomal recessive or dominant mutations in CHRNG gene
Mutations in acetylcholine receptor subunit genes
other: Electromyography may show decreased neuromuscular transmission
Prenatal ultrasound may detect joint contractures and pterygia

distinguishingFeatures: Pterygia primarily limited to popliteal region
Presence of cleft lip and lip pits

redFlags: Severe respiratory compromise due to thoracic cage abnormalities
Progressive joint contractures leading to functional impairment
Feeding difficulties causing failure to thrive
references: Toriello HV. Multiple pterygium syndrome. In: GeneReviews. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.
